messages:
sara_support: FYI customer 'Acme Retail' hit repeated 429s ~03:19 UTC but their project quota tile shows ~85% remaining. They say it happened twice within 10m and app was rate-limited. Ticket: https://redwood.support/t/32145 :thinking:

alex_sre: Can you paste one of the failing request IDs + project id? Also did they hit per-project or org limit?

sara_support: project prj_1234. Two request ids: req_8f3b9 and req_8fa2c. Sample curl they sent:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" \\
  -H "X-Request-Id: req_8f3b9" \\
  -d '{"model":"rwd-1-large","input":"hello"}'
```
They included response header: `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` and body was 429 with message `quota exceeded`. Dashboard still shows 85% on project tile.

ingest-monitor-bot: [alert] rate-limit-enforced prj_1234 at 2025-10-28T03:18:47Z (enforced=1, window_ms=600000)

alex_sre: Thanks. Two quick hypotheses: 1) enforcement uses a sliding/rolling window anchored to request timestamps while dashboard uses minute-aligned snapshots -> can observe mismatch near boundaries. 2) aggregation pipeline lag: dashboard tiles are served from a precomputed snapshot that can be up to a few minutes stale during heavy ingest.

matt_billing: Re: aggregation lag — billing counts (invoices) are computed from the canonical token stream (post-ingest) so invoices should not be impacted, but the dashboard snapshot job had a partial deploy at 03:12 UTC that changed snapshot TTL from 2m -> 30s and then rolled back at 03:15. Could have left some workers on older config leading to inconsistent tiles. Noticing ~3-4m skew in similar incidents.

olivia_prod: I rolled the snapshot change back fully at 03:15 but we had a canary group still on the 30s TTL for 3 nodes. Those would show a different per-project tile vs enforcement. Deploy id: deploy-prod-2025-10-28-0312. I'll check the rollout set.

alex_sre: For SRE debugging steps: 1) check quota-service pods for config `QUOTA_SNAPSHOT_TTL` and confirm uniformity. 2) grep logs for `req_8f3b9`/`req_8fa2c` in ingest and enforcement services: `kubectl logs -l app=quota-service | grep req_8f3b9` 3) hit internal debug endpoint on one of the nodes: `GET /internal/quota/debug?project=prj_1234` (will show sliding-window tokens + last_snapshot_ts). Example response snippet we expect: `last_snapshot_ts=1753999900, sliding_window_count=98000, snapshot_count=75000` — if snapshot_count << sliding_window_count that's the mismatch.

sara_support: OK I've sent the two req ids + the debug instructions to the customer and asked them to share `X-Request-Id` headers if they hit again. Customer is a bit upset, asked for ETA. Any quick mitigation we can offer?

alex_sre: Short-term mitigation: 1) temporarily raise per-project rate-limit on enforcement tier for prj_1234 to avoid further 429s (I can do that for 30m) OR 2) enable routing to a fallback model that has higher concurrency. I'll do the raise after ops confirms.

matt_billing: Confirming again invoices unaffected. We'll add note to ticket explaining tile staleness window and that canonical metering used for billing is different.

olivia_prod: I'll instrument a quick rollout to shrink canary surface and force uniform `QUOTA_SNAPSHOT_TTL=120s` across cluster. Pushing change now and will report back in ~5m. :rocket:

sara_support: thanks all — I'll update the customer with the temporary raise offer and let them know engineering is on it. (reacted :eyes:)
